A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EagleVision and retain the same core framework and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching of relocated and revised content.

before.justification: V1 reports original VSI-Bench results and architecture, reward and hyperparameter ablations in Tables 1–4 and A6.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds SQA3D results in Table 1 and pose-noise/backend experiments in Table 6.

M1.justification: The SPF-DPP, BEV retrieval and GRPO pipeline is retained. V2 absorbs the spatial penalty's alpha_s scale into lambda_spatial and uses retrieval threshold tau_s for the penalty, whereas v1 separately names theta_sim. The PDFs do not establish whether unifying these thresholds changes behavior or only repairs inconsistent notation.

E1.justification: V2 adds SQA3D situated question answering to the original VSI-Bench coverage and mentions SQA3D among training sources. It also evaluates perturbed camera trajectories. These extend task coverage and input conditions beyond the original evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Struct2D, Spatial-Mind and Spatial-MLLM to the VSI-Bench comparison and reports them on SQA3D. It removes InternVL2-40B, LLaVA-NeXT-Video-72B, LLaVA-OneVision-72B, SpaceR-7B and VILASR-7B. This substantially revises comparator membership, while retaining Qwen3-VL-8B and VLM-3R-7B.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify SQA3D validation EM@1, three Gaussian pose-noise levels and a VGGT backend setting. The bandwidth sweep changes its reported alpha from 0.7 in v1 Table A6 to 0.5 in v2 Table 5, without changed scores or evidence of reruns. The original training budget remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct tests of dependence on pose accuracy and reconstruction backend: three trajectory-noise levels and replacement of Vipe with VGGT in Table 6. Existing component and reward ablations remain. The hyperparameter study is relocated from appendix Table A6 to main-text Table 5, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The unchanged 16 rollouts per training prompt concern GRPO training, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds SQA3D EM@1 results: EagleVision 60.3, Struct2D 58.5, Spatial-MLLM 55.9 and Spatial-Mind 46.3. Table 6 adds pose-noise scores of 63.3, 63.1 and 62.9, plus 63.2 with VGGT. EagleVision's original VSI-Bench score remains 63.5; the stated margin over VLM-3R's unchanged 60.9 is corrected from 3.6 to 2.6 points.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1's linear-in-frame diffusion-complexity assertion and explicit O(kN r_bar + k^2 N) runtime claim. It retains the kernel mathematics and the 1-1/e approximation claim but omits the previous monotone-submodular qualification. No new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion extend the state-of-the-art claim from VSI-Bench to both VSI-Bench and SQA3D, explicitly claiming cross-benchmark generalization. The central contributions—dual-stage reasoning, SPF-DPP and reinforcement-learned BEV querying—remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 adds arguments for amortized efficiency through a reusable offline spatial index, backend independence, and robustness because nearest-frame retrieval buffers pose drift. It interprets SQA3D results as transfer and revises the hyperparameter-sensitivity discussion. V1's closing acknowledgment that dependence on external models should be reduced is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page address, identifies the VLM-3R training split and SQA3D training source, asserts separation from test data, and clarifies reusable offline preprocessing and reward provenance. Existing hardware, training budgets, appendix reconstruction details, default hyperparameters and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands from two spatial-model families to three, adding structured 2D approaches and discussion of Struct2D, SpatialMind and Spatial-MLLM. Positioning emphasizes active view acquisition as the distinguishing capability. V2 also adds the standard DPP reference, explicitly attributes task rewards to DeepEyes, and substantially revises the bibliography.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, experimental discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 repairs the method-section hierarchy, condenses and moves the appendix sensitivity discussion into the main text, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an SQA3D column and revised rows; Table 6 is new, and appendix Table A6 moves to main-text Table 5. Ablation tables are rearranged and captions revised. The framework diagrams, qualitative examples and appendix point-cloud figure retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity, corrects the VLM-3R margin and adds useful evidence beyond the original single benchmark, including pose-noise and backend checks. The net gain is limited by stronger interpretations than the new evidence establishes: SQA3D also appears in training, noise percentages are insufficiently specified, and amortized-efficiency claims lack timing measurements.
